name: usage-gauge
description: Two rows under the prompt: model and effort chips in the Anthropic brand blue and orange (a symbol for the level), each turning the theme's warning colour and reading "selected → sent" when a main request does not send the model or effort you selected in /model, /effort, env or settings (checked at session start and on each request; subagents are not compared; between requests a new pick shows within 15 seconds in the plain colours), one clock chip with the session time and how long the prompt cache stays warm (⏱ 1h 12m ⏳ 52m: a dash before the first response, the theme's warning and error as the cache runs low, cold once its lifetime has passed), cost, output speed, tokens in/out, and a git chip: the branch, then three slots (↓ to pull, ± to commit, ↑ to push; a dim ?n for files git does not track yet); context, 5-hour and weekly limits as 10-cell bars in Claude Code's own bar colour (its warning from 70%, its error from 90%) with reset times; the context bar also shows the tokens held. The git chip only reads: git status every 15 seconds and after each turn, and a fetch every 5 minutes so ↓ is current (it writes git's remote-tracking refs, never your files). The branch name takes the room the pane leaves and is cut with … to fit. Each item on row 1 can be turned off in /config. Reads usage figures only; adds no tokens.

showTime.title: Session time
showTime.description: Row 1: how long the session has run, in the clock chip.

showCost.title: Cost
showCost.description: Row 1: the session's cost so far, at API prices.

showSpeed.title: Output speed
showSpeed.description: Row 1: tokens per second of the latest reply.

showTokens.title: Tokens in/out
showTokens.description: Row 1: the session's input and output token counts. With the git chip on, a pane narrower than 131 columns drops them to make room.

showGit.title: Git slots
showGit.description: Row 1: the branch, then ↓ commits to pull, ± files to commit, ↑ commits to push. Reads the repository the session sits in; draws nothing outside one.

showCache.title: Cache timer
showCache.description: Row 1: how long the prompt cache stays warm, in the clock chip after the session time.

fetchRemote.title: Fetch the remote
fetchRemote.description: Run git fetch every 5 minutes so ↓ shows what the remote has now. A fetch writes git's remote-tracking refs and nothing in your working tree. Off: ↓ is as of your last fetch. Needs the git slots on.
